jp: この店[みせ]のケーキは人気[にんき]だから、夕方[ゆうがた]にはもう売[う]り切[き]れている{かもしれません|pt-deshou}。
en: The cakes at this shop are popular, so they might already be sold out by evening.
why: A possibility the speaker cannot confirm takes かもしれません; the others express intention or timing.

jp: 給料日[きゅうりょうび]の前[まえ]だから、田中[たなか]さんの財布[さいふ]にはもうお金[かね]があまりない{でしょう|pt-deshou}。
en: Since it's just before payday, Mr. Tanaka's wallet probably has little money left.
why: An inference about something the speaker cannot see is expressed with でしょう; the others state past timing or a decision.

jp: このスーパーは野菜[やさい]がとても安[やす]い{でしょう|pt-deshou}？ だからよく来[く]るんです。
en: The vegetables at this supermarket are really cheap, aren't they? That's why I come here often.
why: Rising でしょう asks the listener to agree with something; the other endings do not attach to an adjective here.

jp: 今日[きょう]は定休日[ていきゅうび]だから、あの八百屋[やおや]はきっと閉[し]まっている{だろう|pt-deshou}。
en: Today is their regular day off, so that greengrocer is surely closed.
why: A plain-style guess based on a known reason is だろう; the others express intention or a decision.

jp: 台風[たいふう]のせいで、来月[らいげつ]は野菜[やさい]の値段[ねだん]がもっと上[あ]がる{かもしれません|pt-deshou}。
en: Because of the typhoon, vegetable prices might rise even more next month.
why: Next month's prices are uncertain, so the speaker names only a possibility; the others state a plan, a decision or timing.

jp: 夜遅[よるおそ]くにラーメンを食[た]べると、太[ふと]る{かもしれません|pt-deshou}よ。
en: If you eat ramen late at night, you might gain weight.
why: A warning about something that may happen takes かもしれません; the others are decisions, intentions or timing.
